text:
alex: Quick heads-up — we've got a customer report where v1 clients are getting charged twice when a version-pin + console cache hit occurs. Looks like pinning prevents route fallthrough but cache keys don't include version so quota attribution duplicates.

nina: ugh. that's going to skew billing dashboards and the per-route cost numbers. any repro?

alex: repro attached (short stack): pinned header -> routing layer picks v1 -> cache key (model+prompt hash) hits -> telemetry emitted for both the incoming route and the cached response path. script: `curl -H "x-redwood-version: v1" ...` reproduces.

sam: can we just include the version in the cache key as a short-term fix? Seems like lowest blast radius.

lee: including version would be safest for correctness but could reduce cache efficiency if clients often vary versions in calls. tradeoff.

marco: alternative: change telemetry attribution so cached responses attribute to the original serving route only, not both. that avoids changing caching behavior.

alex: both options have downsides. changing telemetry is less risky runtime-wise but makes billing weird for historical comparisons. adding version to keys changes hit rate.

nina: how often do we see mixed-version cache hits? low sample in prod, but a few high-volume tenants pin v1. console shows a spike in v1 token count + overall tokens.

sam: proposal: 1) short-term: add version to cache key for pinned requests only 2) medium: emit a stable attribution event that says "served_via_cache_for_version" and use that for billing pipeline 3) long-term: console UX to surface pin+cache interactions and expected cost delta.

lee: for short-term patch, fwiw we should also add a feature flag + rollout so we can flip back if cache hit rate collapses.

marco: agreed. I'll draft the telemetry event change so billing can consult a single canonical field instead of summing two signals.

alex: ok owner matrix: marco -> telemetry schema + billing mapping, sam -> caching key changes + feature flag, lee -> runtime rollout, nina -> console UX copy and banner, alex -> coordinate comms and docs.

deploy-bot: Canary job queued: routing-cache-key-patch v1-pinned -> start in 10m.

nina: for the console banner, suggest: "We detected pinned model versions affecting cache efficiency. This can change billing estimates. See details -> link." keep short.

sam: quick config snippet for the flag: ```yaml
feature_flags:
  versioned_cache_for_pins: on: false rollout: 10% buckets: user_id_hash
```

lee: timeline idea: patch -> canary 10% (24h) -> monitor token hit rate + latency -> 50% (48h) -> billing samples validated -> full.

marco: telemetry query I'll need: one-time mapping from raw logs to canonical attribution. sam, can you tag the cache write with `origin_version` in logs? makes backfilling easier.

sam: yep will add `origin_version` tag to cache writes + `served_version` to responses.

alex: thanks. Nina, can you draft console copy + a small tooltip explaining "why my v1 usage jumped"? keep it non-technical.

nina: on it. i'll put a draft in /docs/console/alerts and ping here.

marco: I'll update billing ETL once we have the canary logs, aim for a non-invasive mapping so historical dashboards don't break.

alex: perfect. let's reconvene in 24h in this thread. if anyone hits a blocker, @alex and @sam. :thumbsup:

sam: noted. will post canary metrics (hit rate, latency, tokens attributed) as they come.

lee: one more thought — for future: consider console toggle to show costs with "version-aware caching" vs "legacy" for tenant-facing estimates. but that's R&D.

alex: agreed, add to backlog after this stabilizes. thanks all.
